risks.note: Gold jewellery accounted for 92.33%, 94.58% and 93.96% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Higher international gold prices, higher import duties, regulatory restrictions, a decline in discretionary spending or a shift in consumer preference would hit almost the entire revenue base.

The Company does not employ hedging practices such as gold metal loan facilities, forward contracts or options, unlike most of its competitors, so it is directly exposed to gold price fluctuations on both inventory value and demand. Jewellery purchases are discretionary and rising gold prices can cause customers to defer buying.

The jewellery business requires substantial gold and diamond inventory: inventory was 96.81% of total current assets in Fiscal 2026 and 39.23% of revenue from operations (versus 34.76% in Fiscal 2025 and 25.57% in Fiscal 2024). Working capital rose to Rs 44,661.08 million and working capital days to 65; inventory turnover fell to 2.55x from 2.88x and 3.91x. Delays in inventory turnover or adverse gold/diamond price moves can force write-downs and stretch liquidity.
risks.risk: Working capital intensity and inventory risk

business_ops.seasonality: Demand for jewellery in India is mainly driven by weddings, festivals, births and the harvest season; buying jewellery during festivals such as Diwali, Dussehra and Akshaya Tritiya is considered auspicious, producing significant purchase spikes, and demand is also high through the wedding season (Source: CRISIL Report). The Company states its sales in certain regions have historically exhibited seasonal fluctuations with higher volumes during festival periods and occasions such as Akshaya Tritiya, Durga Puja, Dhanteras, Diwali, Poila and Baisakh, which also coincide with the Indian wedding season. 'Diwali' and 'Dhanteras' are described as the biggest jewellery buying festivals, during which the Company's sales and marketing effort generally spikes; it capitalises on Akshaya Tritiya to promote sales - for example offering 2% and 3% less on making charges for gold and Rs 6,000 less per carat on carat prices for diamond jewellery from April 12, 2025 to May 4, 2025. Marketing schemes are tailored to occasion, season and customer need (weddings, anniversaries, birthdays), and inventory is planned season-by-season with stock built ahead of peak periods. The Company flags that fixed costs - lease rentals, employee salaries, store operating costs and logistics expenses, which form a significant portion of operating costs - remain relatively constant through the year, so lower-than-expected sales in peak quarters would have a disproportionate impact on full-year operating results and could strain resources and impair cash flows; consequently quarter-on-quarter results may not be comparable or a meaningful indicator of performance. The Company states it has not so far faced such a slowdown in demand or a failure to anticipate seasonal fluctuations, but gives no assurance for the future.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward-integrated, asset-light retail model. Raw material vendors supply gold bullion, silver, diamonds and precious/semi-precious stones, which the Company purchases directly (gold bullion from bullion traders; diamonds mostly from diamond traders and sightholders) on the basis of tax invoices, through purchase orders and without long-term supplier agreements. The Company then supplies raw materials to Karigars (in-house and external) who manufacture jewellery to the Company's designs or designs approved by it, against making charges; the finished jewellery returns to the Company, is hallmarked and quality-checked, and is sold through its own stores - the Company describes itself as 'engaged in the complete value chain of the manufacturing process from designing of jewellery to selling of finished products'. Karigars manufacture more than 79% of products. Two owned/subsidiary Manufacturing Facilities support this: Thirumudivakkam, Chennai (approx. 43,861.96 sq. ft., operations commenced December 2, 2024) run by the Company, and Maraimalainagar, Kanchipuram (approx. 20,000 sq. ft.) run by wholly owned subsidiary Asita Jewellery Manufacturing Private Limited. As of March 31, 2026 the facilities are worked by 816 Karigars on exclusive arrangements and on the rolls of the Company (672 with the Company, 144 with Asita), plus 296 Karigars under short-term non-exclusive agreements. In-house manufacturing is stated to reduce jewellery-making wastage and allow lower value-addition charges to be passed to customers without compromising margins. Old jewellery exchanged or sold back by customers is re-used as raw material, and the Company procures old gold from customers to encourage repeat business. Quality assurance runs two checkpoints before a piece reaches a showroom - an internal quality control department checking purity and finish, then an external government-approved hallmarking centre operating to BIS norms; all loose diamonds are tested by a testing agency and all diamond products certified by an accredited laboratory; finished Karigar output is re-checked for gold, diamond and gemstone quality and design finish. Inventory is bar-coded at all locations and monitored manually and through the 'JILABA ERP' system which carries a built-in inventory management module and gives virtual connectivity across all stores and offices; stock levels are reviewed daily with replenishment action and supply chain is planned season-by-season. Inventory is carried at the lower of net realisable value and cost (annual weighted average cost for gold, silver and diamonds); as at March 31, 2026 gold inventory was Rs 86,830.29 million (Rs 868,302.9 lakhs), silver Rs 8,221.54 million (Rs 82,215.4 lakhs) and diamond and precious/semi-precious stones Rs 3,110.92 million (Rs 31,109.2 lakhs). Total inventory was Rs 98,162.76 million (Rs 981,627.6 lakhs) in FY2026, Rs 58,727.29 million (Rs 587,272.9 lakhs) in FY2025 and Rs 42,920.80 million (Rs 429,208.0 lakhs) in FY2024, with inventory turnover ratio of 2.55, 2.88 and 3.91 times respectively. Downstream, the model is asset-light: of 61 stores only three are owned and the rest are on leave-and-licence; distribution is entirely through own-brand 'Lalithaa' stores supported by in-house sales teams speaking regional languages, a customer-care mobile app, jeweller's block insurance on all goods movement, and insurance coverage at 81.04% of total tangible assets as at March 31, 2026. Working capital is part-funded by customer advances under the jewellery schemes (Rs 50,427.50 million / 20.15% of revenue in FY2026). Employees numbered 7,059 as of March 31, 2026 (senior management 11, managers 430, sales 3,979, security 195, administration 59, back office 1,222, others 1,163), with total attrition of 30.90%, 27.84% and 35.67% in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 (FY2026 by function: senior management Nil, manager 17.21%, sales 33.83%, security 16.41%, administration 38.98%, back office 35.02%, others 23.90%).

Covenants require lender consent for additional debt, prepayment, dividends, capex beyond thresholds, changes to constitutional documents, capital structure, shareholding or management, and disposal of encumbered assets; some lenders can convert outstandings into fully paid-up Equity Shares on default, and cross-default provisions apply (RF 4, RF 14).
financial_valuation.evidence: Total outstanding borrowing of Rs 12,381.00 mn as on June 30, 2026 towards term loan and working capital loan facilities. 'As on the date of the RHP, we have complied with all such conditions and covenants' - but also 'We cannot assure you that we have complied with all such covenants in a timely manner or at all'. Financial covenants include specified debt-to-equity ratios.
financial_valuation.title: Outstanding borrowings of Rs 12,381.00 million and restrictive financing covenants

internal_operational.detail: Sale of gold jewellery is the overwhelming majority of revenue from operations; silver jewellery/articles and 'others' (silverware and diamond jewellery) are marginal. Any increase in international gold prices, higher import duties, regulatory restrictions, fall in discretionary spending or shift in preference away from gold hits the bulk of revenue (RF 1).
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentration in gold jewellery

internal_operational.detail: The company changes jewellery designs regularly but does not register them, so it cannot readily enforce IP in its designs; Karigars making more than 79% of products may make the same or similar jewellery for competitors. Fashion/consumer-preference misjudgement can depress demand (RF 6).
internal_operational.evidence: Design team of fifteen members as at March 31, 2026 (CAD and manual designers at Thirumudivakkam, Tamil Nadu); spend on designing activities Rs 10.42 mn, Rs 9.63 mn and Rs 4.55 mn over the last three Fiscals; Karigars produce more than 79% of products.
internal_operational.title: Designs are not registered under the Design Act, 2000 and design refresh risk

internal_operational.detail: Gold is procured on purchase orders without long-term agreements and the top three suppliers account for the majority of raw-material cost, with a single supplier over half in FY26. Loss of a supplier or supply interruption would impair production and delivery (RF 10).
internal_operational.title: Raw-material supplier concentration; no long-term supply agreements

concerns_observed: Fiscal 2026's 48.09% revenue increase is attributed by the RHP itself to price, not volume or footprint: 'an increase in number of stores from 60 stores in Financial Year 2025 to 61 stores in Financial Year 2026', 'increase in average rate of gold from Rs 7.33 million per kilogram during Financial Year 2025 to Rs 10.63 million per kilogram during Financial Year 2026' and 'increase in sale of gold from 21,531.77 kilograms in Financial Year 2025 to 21,691.43 kilograms in Financial Year 2026'. Gold volume in Fiscal 2024 was 26,018.75 kilograms on 53 stores, i.e. above the Fiscal 2026 tonnage on 61 stores. The Company's own disclosed market share in the southern states fell from 6.46% (FY24) to 5.13% (FY25) to 4.97% (FY26).

Operating cash flow was negative in the year of highest reported profit: net cash used in operating activities Rs 3,977.62 mn in Fiscal 2026 and Rs 180.02 mn in Fiscal 2024, against generation of Rs 2,887.31 mn in Fiscal 2025, while PAT ran Rs 3,598.33 / 3,647.26 / 10,098.17 mn. Fiscal 2026 was funded by a financing inflow of Rs 4,277.30 mn (net short-term borrowings Rs 6,674.68 mn); cash and cash equivalents closed at Rs 161.09 mn against Rs 523.19 mn a year earlier, and the restated cash flow carries an increase in inventories of Rs 39,435.47 mn.

The balance sheet is inventory, and it is unhedged: inventory Rs 42,920.80 mn (FY24) to Rs 58,727.29 mn (FY25) to Rs 98,162.76 mn (FY26), being 25.57% / 34.76% / 39.23% of revenue and 96.74% / 96.02% / 96.81% of current assets, with inventory turnover falling 3.91 to 2.88 to 2.55 times and inventory days rising 93 to 127 to 143. Risk Factor 41 states 'we do not employ hedging practices such as availing gold metal loans facilities unlike the practices most of our competitors employ' - no gold metal loans, forward contracts or options - while the average monthly high gold price moved from Rs 65,229 (FY24) to Rs 86,890 (FY25) to Rs 154,039 (FY26) per 10 grams.

The Fresh Issue is predominantly inventory funding presented as store expansion: of the Rs 12,000 mn Fresh Issue, Rs 10,332.31 mn goes to 10 New Stores, of which Rs 9,986.81 mn is opening-day inventory and only Rs 345.50 mn is fit-out capital expenditure (per-store estimate at an assumed 11,000 sq. ft., certified by Aini Designs, Independent Architect, July 24, 2026). No specific locations have been identified, no binding agreements or lease/licence agreements for the New Store sites have been executed, and store lease security deposits and advance rentals are to come from internal accruals, not the Net Proceeds. All 16 fit-out and equipment line items are unplaced quotations (Aini Designs July 24, 2026; all others May 30, 2026), with the RHP stating 'we have not entered into any definitive agreements with the contractor/ vendor'. The deployment is not appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency, and the general corporate purposes amount is [.].

Ownership is effectively a single holder and part of the Offer takes money out, not in: the Promoters hold 488,574,156 Equity Shares (97.72%) pre-Offer, the Company has only 34 Shareholders as on the date of the RHP, and the Offer for Sale of up to Rs 5,000 mn of the Rs 17,000 mn Offer accrues entirely to the Promoter Selling Shareholder M. Kiran Kumar Jain, not the Company. The Promoters' average cost of acquisition on a fully diluted basis is Rs 3.51 and Rs 1.25 against a face value of Rs 5; the weighted average cost of acquisition of all shares transacted in the last three years is Rs 0.45 with a range of Rs 0-1,374 (certified by R.K. Chapawat & Co., August 9, 2026). The 20:1 bonus of 476,168,720 Equity Shares on June 24, 2024 took capital from 23,808,436 to 499,977,156 shares.

Both Subsidiaries were purchased from the Promoter, one of them a nil-revenue apparels entity: under SPAs each dated April 1, 2024 with M. Kiran Kumar Jain as Seller, the Company paid Rs 745.47 mn for 99.98% of Asita Jewellery Manufacturing Private Limited at Rs 74,562 per share (disclosed NAV per share Rs 12,110.42 and PAT Rs 10.97 mn at March 31, 2024), and Rs 289.59 mn for 99.98% of Centigrade Apparels Private Limited at Rs 2,896 per share (disclosed NAV per share Rs 165.16 at March 31, 2024). Centigrade printed nil revenue from operations and losses of Rs 0.13 mn (FY24), Rs 2.98 mn (FY25) and Rs 0.92 mn (FY26), with net asset value of Rs 12.61 mn at March 31, 2026. Valuations by Vivro Financial Services Private Limited, registered valuer; the Fiscal 2025 cash flow carries 'payment towards acquisition of entities of Rs 975.22 million'.

A Promoter Group entity in the same line of business is also a material supplier: A. K. Exports, the sole proprietorship of Promoter M. Kiran Kumar Jain, 'operates in a similar line of business' and 'deals with certain common vendors' (RF 37). Purchases from AK Exports Rs 3,645.49 mn / 2.17% of revenue (FY24), Rs 3,506.70 mn / 2.08% (FY25) and Rs 3,678.14 mn / 1.47% (FY26); sales to AK Exports Rs 125.74 / 287.72 / 84.29 mn; year-end payable Rs 0.45 mn (FY24), Rs 785.15 mn (FY25) and Rs 432.58 mn (FY26).

Promoter compensation was restructured across the reported period without a stated basis: in Fiscal 2024 the two Promoter directors drew nil remuneration while M. Kiran Kumar Jain was paid Rs 502.76 mn (0.30% of revenue) in brand ambassador fees under a Brand Endorsement Agreement dated April 1, 2019 running to March 31, 2031 at Rs 253.00 mn per annum with escalation, waived partially for Fiscal 2022 and fully for Fiscal 2023 and terminated with effect from April 1, 2024; in each of Fiscals 2025 and 2026 directors' remuneration was Rs 120.00 mn (M. Kiran Kumar Jain) and Rs 90.00 mn (Hemaa Kiran Kumar Jain), against Rs 3.15 mn for the third Whole-time Director and Rs 2.42 mn for the Chief Financial Officer in Fiscal 2026. The related-party disclosure excludes gratuity because separate actuarial valuations are not available.

Rent paid to the Promoters jumped in Fiscal 2026 on agreements dated 2016: rent to M. Kiran Kumar Jain Rs 36.46 mn (FY24), Rs 37.73 mn (FY25) and Rs 179.76 mn (FY26) with a year-end payable of Rs 16.03 mn, and to Hemaa Kiran Kumar Jain Rs 2.40 / 2.40 / 17.34 mn, under lease agreements dated August 25, 2016 and June 1, 2016 for Panjagutta, Hyderabad and 53 Habibullah Road, T. Nagar, Chennai. Security deposits receivable from M. Kiran Kumar Jain stood at Rs 365.15 mn and from Hemaa Kiran Kumar Jain at Rs 85.25 mn at March 31, 2026.

Raw-material supply is concentrating into one counterparty with no contracts: Supplier 1 alone accounted for Rs 46,048.51 mn / 36.81% of raw-material cost (FY24), Rs 62,123.44 mn / 47.67% (FY25) and Rs 98,832.07 mn / 50.44% (FY26); top three 66.98% / 67.20% / 58.03% and top ten 76.57% / 75.53% / 69.38%. Gold is procured on purchase orders with no long-term agreements with suppliers, and certain supplier names are withheld because consents were not provided.

The audit trail failed on the system that carries the inventory: the auditor reports that the edit-log feature of the Jilaba system used to maintain sales and inventory records 'did not operate throughout the financial year ended March 31, 2026', so the auditor cannot comment on whether it was tampered with - for the system holding the stock that is 96.81% of current assets. Alongside, CARO clause vii(a) records undisputed statutory dues outstanding beyond six months at March 31, 2026 of Rs 619.25 mn (advance-tax instalments for the quarter ended September 30, 2025), and delayed statutory dues of 327 instances / Rs 22.43 mn (FY24), 355 / Rs 5.11 mn (FY25) and 197 / Rs 2.80 mn (FY26).

The corporate record is incomplete for a company incorporated in 1985: Form-2 returns of allotment, Form 32, Form 62, committee-constitution resolutions, certain board and shareholders' resolutions and copies of certain transfer deeds for Equity Share transfers by and to the Promoters are not traceable with the Company or the RoC, and reliance is placed on certificates dated June 6, 2025 and August 9, 2026 from RLS & Associates, practising company secretary. The Register of Members also incorrectly records the July 1, 1986 and April 2, 1987 allotments, and the PAS-3 for the June 24, 2024 bonus carried a clerical error re-filed on May 13, 2025.

SEBI-adjacent history sits on both Promoters and on a Promoter Group entity: SEBI issued summons each dated February 9, 2022 to M. Kiran Kumar Jain and Hemaa Kiran Kumar Jain alleging that transactions in the scrip of Krishana Fabrics Limited - in which they hold majority equity - were dealt with in a manner detrimental to investors or the securities market, in violation of the SEBI Act and Insider Trading Regulations (replied February 16, 2022 and August 10, 2024; no proceedings initiated as on date). Separately, Dilip Chhabria Design Private Limited is deemed Promoter Group, is under liquidation, and SEBI by letter dated March 19, 2025 refused the Regulation 300(1)(c) exemption sought on October 7, 2024, so disclosures for it rest on MCA, CIBIL, BSE, NSE, SEBI and Watchout Investors sources rather than the entity.

The GST matter is stayed, not resolved, and is carried at less than the order amount: an order dated January 8, 2025 confirmed a demand of Rs 533.17 mn with an equivalent penalty, a total liability of Rs 1,066.38 mn, arising from excess input tax credit availed 'due to typo error during the financial year 2017-18'; Form GST DRC-07 dated January 30, 2025 continued to reflect the full Rs 1,066.38 mn. The Order-in-Appeal of January 2026 set aside interest on the unutilised Rs 512.46 mn but upheld interest on the Rs 20.71 mn utilised, and the High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Amaravati stayed recovery by writ of Certiorari on March 11, 2026. Rs 538.19 mn (including interest of Rs 4.97 mn) is disclosed as contingent liability, outflow assessed as remote and no provision recognised.

Guarantees given for the Company exceed the Company's own disclosed borrowings: total borrowings secured by personal guarantees of the Promoters and a Promoter Group member are Rs 17,597.33 mn as of June 30, 2026 against total outstanding borrowings of Rs 12,381.00 mn on the same date; a joint guarantee by the Directors and Group Company Lalitha Castle Private Limited stood at Rs 9,270 mn (FY24), Rs 10,555 mn (FY25) and Rs 17,000 mn (FY26), with the RHP stating that individual amounts are not available. Balance-sheet borrowings were Rs 8,241.77 mn (FY24), Rs 9,492.58 mn (FY25) and Rs 16,041.36 mn (FY26), the increase attributed in MD&A to launching new stores in a year in which the store count moved from 60 to 61.

Scheme enrolment stopped growing while the liability it creates nearly doubled: active enrolled scheme customers 398,762 (FY24), 475,911 (FY25) and 473,412 (FY26) against advances from customers of Rs 19,432.26 / 31,454.10 / 50,427.50 mn; other current liabilities, almost entirely these contract liabilities, stand at Rs 51,238.31 mn at March 31, 2026 versus Rs 31,982.04 mn a year earlier, settleable in jewellery and carrying bonus and value-addition-discount obligations.

Governance depth is thin for a company of this size: only one of six Directors (Nayan Jagadishchandra Rawal) has prior experience as a director of a listed Indian company; two Independent Directors appointed on January 8, 2024 resigned within months (Qudsia Gandhi on February 17, 2024, Manik Lal Karmakar on April 10, 2024); the Audit Committee of three includes executive Promoter director Hemaa Kiran Kumar Jain, whose qualification is stated as 'She has not received formal education' and whose Fiscal 2026 remuneration was Rs 90.00 mn; and the Promoters and Promoter Group will retain majority control post-Offer over strategy, mergers, dividend policy and capital structure. Total employee attrition was 35.67% (FY24), 27.84% (FY25) and 30.90% (FY26).

Insurance cover fell below the asset base in the year the asset base grew fastest: cover was 113.39% of total assets at March 31, 2024 and 110.11% at March 31, 2025 but 81.04% at March 31, 2026 (insured assets Rs 100,427.70 mn covered to Rs 82,055.01 mn, uninsured Rs 822.13 mn, total assets Rs 101,249.83 mn), and certain policies (Bharat Laghu, Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha) are in the Promoter's name with no underlying assets, leaving the Company dependent on the Promoter for any future claim. Jewellery worth Rs 24.05 mn was stolen from a Chennai store in Fiscal 2021.

The channel is single-mode and the demand backdrop carries a stated policy headwind: all sales are made in person at physical stores, e-commerce operations began only in Fiscal 2023 and are limited to the schemes, and the RHP states 'we currently do not generate any revenue through such online channels'; advertisement and sales promotion spend was 0.49% / 0.45% / 0.33% of revenue across FY24-FY26 with all advertising featuring Promoter M. Kiran Kumar Jain and no external brand ambassador contracted. Risk Factor 35 records that 'In May 2026, the Prime Minister of India publicly urged citizens to refrain from purchasing gold for a period of at least one year'.
data_gaps: Every price-dependent figure is a placeholder: the Price Band, Offer Price, number of Fresh Issue and Offer for Sale shares, post-Offer issued and paid-up capital, post-Offer shareholding percentages, securities premium after the Offer, the issuer's P/E, and the Floor Price and Cap Price multiples of the weighted average cost of acquisition. No market capitalisation, P/E or valuation conclusion can be formed from this document, and none has been.

The Promoters' Contribution lock-in table - shares held, shares locked in, dates of allotment or transfer, acquisition price, percentage of post-Offer fully diluted capital and the date up to which locked in - is printed entirely as [.], so no lock-in expiry date is stated. Only the periods are given: three years for 20% of post-Offer capital, one year for the excess, six months for other pre-Offer capital, and 90/30 days for anchor tranches.

No capacity or capacity-utilisation table exists anywhere in the RHP - neither installed capacity nor utilisation percentage for either manufacturing facility. Manufacturing is Karigar-labour based; the nearest volume disclosures are gold sold (21,691.43 / 21,531.77 / 26,018.75 kilograms) and gold purchased (17,442.94 kg in FY25, 19,917.77 kg in FY24).

No customer-concentration table is disclosed - the Company is a business-to-consumer retailer selling to walk-in customers. The 'Top 10 customers' row on page 30 sits inside a table headed '% of total cost of raw materials' and is a supplier figure, not a customer figure.

Financial details of the Group Companies Lalitha Castle Private Limited and Krishkiran Mega Mall Private Limited - reserves, sales/income, profit, EPS and NAV for the preceding three years - are hosted only on the Company's website and are not set out in the RHP.

The individual split of the Rs 17,000 mn joint guarantee provided by the Directors and Lalitha Castle Private Limited is stated as not available, and directors' remuneration in the related-party note excludes gratuity because separate actuarial valuations are not available.
No domestic/export split, no B2B/B2C split and no online revenue percentage are disclosed; the RHP states only that online channels currently generate no revenue.

No order book, orders in hand or contracted customer value exists - the nearest analogue is the Rs 50,427.50 mn of customer scheme advances, which is a deposit liability the RHP describes as giving 'visibility of sales in subsequent periods', not a contracted order book.

The composition of the IPO Committee is not disclosed, and debtor days, inventory days and creditor days are given only through the composite working-capital days figure of 65 / 56 / 50 for FY26 / FY25 / FY24.

Internal inconsistencies remain unreconciled in the document itself: the Thirumudivakkam facility area is 43,861.96 sq. ft. in Our Business and Property but 43,681.96 sq. ft. in MD&A; Karnataka's Fiscal 2024 revenue share is 11.32% in one table and 11.33% in another; operating EBITDA per store for Fiscal 2026 is 274.34 in one table and 274.35 in another; the 2023 e4m award is dated 2023 in one section and 2024 in another; and MD&A cites an average head count of 8,853 (FY25) and 9,077 (FY26) against a stated year-end employee strength of 7,059.

Financial statements are prepared under Ind AS with no reconciliation to, or quantification of the impact of, Indian GAAP, IFRS or US GAAP (RF 58), and capital commitments are not disclosed in the contingent-liability note.

Industry data comes solely from the CRISIL Report titled 'Assessment of the global and Indian gems and jewellery market' dated July 2026, commissioned and paid for by the Company exclusively for the Offer and disclosed only as excerpts, so the market-share, per-store and 'largest store' claims rest on a report the issuer procured.
monitorables: Gold volume rather than gold value: kilograms of gold sold (26,018.75 in FY24, 21,531.77 in FY25, 21,691.43 in FY26) against store count 53 / 60 / 61, and the gap between average realised rate (Rs 5.96 / 7.33 / 10.63 mn per kilogram) and average purchase rate (Rs 7.21 in FY25, Rs 11.21 mn per kilogram in FY26).
Operating cash flow versus PAT in the first reported period after listing, and whether the Fiscal 2026 outflow of Rs 3,977.62 mn reverses or repeats as inventory continues to build.
Inventory days and turnover (93 / 127 / 143 days and 3.91 / 2.88 / 2.55 times across FY24-FY26) and inventory as a percentage of revenue (25.57% / 34.76% / 39.23%).

Whether the Company begins hedging - gold metal loans, forwards or options - and any change in the Risk Factor 41 position of no hedging, particularly if gold prices reverse from the Rs 154,039 per 10 grams average monthly high of Fiscal 2026.

Progress of the 10 New Stores: sites identified, lease or licence agreements executed, quotations converted into orders (all 16 line items were unplaced quotations valid six months from May 30 and July 24, 2026), and actual against the Rs 5,166.15 mn per year deployment in Fiscals 2027 and 2028.

Advances from customers (Rs 50,427.50 mn, 20.15% of revenue) against active enrolled scheme customers (473,412, down from 475,911), and any regulatory development affecting appropriation of scheme advances.

Disposal of the writ petition before the High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Amaravati on the Rs 1,066.38 mn GST demand, the rectification of Form GST DRC-07, and whether the Rs 538.19 mn contingent liability converts to a provision.

Related-party quantum after listing: purchases from A. K. Exports, rent to the Promoters, security deposits receivable from them (Rs 365.15 mn and Rs 85.25 mn at March 31, 2026), and whether Audit Committee approval of these is disclosed with a benchmarking basis.
Restoration of the Jilaba audit trail and closure of the IT-review observations that Risk Factor 40 says the Company 'is in the process of implementing'.
Supplier 1's share of raw-material cost (36.81% to 47.67% to 50.44%) and whether any long-term supply agreement is executed.
Insurance cover as a percentage of total assets (113.39% / 110.11% / 81.04%) and whether the Promoter-name policies are transferred to the Company.
Borrowings and covenant headroom: Rs 16,041.36 mn at March 31, 2026 falling to Rs 12,381.00 mn at June 30, 2026, the specified debt-to-equity covenants, and the ICRA A (Stable) rating.
Employee attrition (35.67% / 27.84% / 30.90%) and Karigar retention - 816 exclusive Karigars produce 79.11% of products and 296 more work on cancellable short-term non-exclusive agreements.

Whether the Company begins to earn revenue from its website and mobile application, currently stated to generate none, and the demand effect of the May 2026 public appeal to refrain from purchasing gold for at least a year.
Board build-out after listing: addition of directors with listed-company experience, Audit Committee composition, and whether the Company Secretary and CFO functions are strengthened.
open_questions: How much of the Fiscal 2026 operating EBITDA margin move from 4.38% to 6.69% is holding gain on inventory carried at annual weighted average cost during a year in which the average monthly high gold price went from Rs 86,890 to Rs 154,039 per 10 grams, versus operating leverage? The RHP attributes the revenue increase to store count, gold rate and volume but does not attribute the margin.

Why does the RHP print an average gold purchase rate of Rs 11.21 mn per kilogram for Fiscal 2026 above the average realised gold rate of Rs 10.63 mn per kilogram, when Fiscal 2025 printed Rs 7.21 against Rs 7.33? Are the two rates struck on the same basis, and what does the difference imply for the gross margin on Fiscal 2027 sales out of Fiscal 2026-priced stock?

What was the valuation basis for paying the Promoter Rs 289.59 mn (Rs 2,896 per share) for Centigrade Apparels Private Limited, an entity with nil revenue from operations in each of Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026, losses in each year, and a disclosed net asset value per share of Rs 165.16 at March 31, 2024? What role does an apparels entity play in a jewellery group beyond providing land and building as collateral for a bank borrowing?

What drove related-party rent to M. Kiran Kumar Jain from Rs 37.73 mn in Fiscal 2025 to Rs 179.76 mn in Fiscal 2026, and to Hemaa Kiran Kumar Jain from Rs 2.40 mn to Rs 17.34 mn, when the underlying lease agreements are dated August 25, 2016 and June 1, 2016? Was there a rent revision, an added property, or an arrears catch-up, and was it benchmarked to market?

Why are Rs 9,986.81 mn of opening-day inventory for stores whose locations are not yet identified being funded from a Fresh Issue, rather than from the working capital facilities that already fund Rs 98,162.76 mn of existing inventory - and what happens to the deployment schedule if the leases are not signed by Fiscal 2028?

Why did active enrolled scheme customers fall from 475,911 to 473,412 while advances from customers rose from Rs 31,454.10 mn to Rs 50,427.50 mn? Is the increase instalment-size driven, gold-price driven, or is it a lengthening of unredeemed balances - and what is the redemption profile of the Rs 50,427.50 mn?

Single supplier concentration went 36.81% to 47.67% to 50.44% of raw-material cost with no long-term agreement. Who is Supplier 1, is it a related party, and what happens to procurement if that relationship changes?

The Jilaba edit log did not operate for the whole of Fiscal 2026 on the sales and inventory system. When did it stop, when was it restored, what compensating controls covered the period, and does any portion of the Rs 98,162.76 mn closing inventory rest on records without an audit trail?

The Rs 1,066.38 mn GST order remains reflected in full in Form GST DRC-07 while only Rs 538.19 mn is carried as a contingent liability and recovery is stayed. What is the Company's basis for assessing outflow as remote, and what is the exposure if the Andhra Pradesh High Court writ petition fails?

Directors' remuneration excludes gratuity because 'separate actuarial valuation is not available' for the Promoter directors. What is the total cost to company of the two Promoter directors including retirement benefits, and how is Rs 120.00 mn and Rs 90.00 mn set against Fiscal 2026 PAT of Rs 10,098.17 mn?

What is the individual split of the Rs 17,000 mn joint guarantee by the Directors and Lalitha Castle Private Limited, and of the Rs 17,597.33 mn of borrowings secured by personal guarantees - the RHP states individual amounts are not available?

Insurance cover fell from 110.11% of total assets at March 31, 2025 to 81.04% at March 31, 2026 in the year inventory grew from Rs 58,727.29 mn to Rs 98,162.76 mn. Is the shortfall a policy-renewal lag or a deliberate retention, and which asset classes are uncovered?

parameter_scores.basis: Net cash from operating activities of Rs (180.02) mn (FY24), Rs 2,887.31 mn (FY25) and Rs (3,977.62) mn (FY26) against PAT of Rs 3,598.33 / 3,647.26 / 10,098.17 mn - negative in two of three years and most negative in the year of highest reported profit, driven by an increase in inventories of Rs 39,435.47 mn partly offset by an increase in other current liabilities of Rs 19,256.27 mn. Separately, the RHP prints an average gold purchase rate of Rs 11.21 mn per kilogram in Fiscal 2026 against an average realised gold rate of Rs 10.63 mn per kilogram (Fiscal 2025: Rs 7.21 against Rs 7.33); the document does not state that the two rates are drawn on a comparable basis.

Risk Factor 41 confirms no gold metal loans, forward contracts or options, unlike most competitors, while gold moved from Rs 60,624 to Rs 75,842 to Rs 115,996 per 10 grams (average monthly high Rs 65,229 to Rs 86,890 to Rs 154,039). Inventory is carried at lower of net realisable value and annual weighted average cost.

Kiran Kumar Jain under SPAs dated April 1, 2024 - Asita for Rs 745.47 mn at Rs 74,562 per share (NAV per share Rs 12,110.42, PAT Rs 10.97 mn at March 31, 2024) and Centigrade Apparels for Rs 289.59 mn at Rs 2,896 per share (NAV per share Rs 165.16), the latter with nil revenue from operations and losses in each of FY24, FY25 and FY26. strengths_observed: Reported profitability stepped up sharply in Fiscal 2026 on all three printed lines: revenue from operations Rs 167,880.52 mn (FY24) to Rs 168,973.17 mn (FY25) to Rs 250,239.27 mn (FY26); operating EBITDA Rs 6,801.67 / 7,403.59 / 16,735.04 mn at margins of 4.05% / 4.38% / 6.69%; PAT Rs 3,598.33 / 3,647.26 / 10,098.17 mn at margins of 2.14% / 2.16% / 4.04%; basic and diluted EPS Rs 7.20 / 7.29 / 20.20 and NAV per share Rs 58.60.

Return ratios sit at or above the top of the RHP's own peer table: Fiscal 2026 ROE 41.60%, ROCE 42.60% and RoNW 39.90%, against peer RoNW of Titan 36.48%, Thangamayil 27.93%, Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri 27.06%, Senco Gold 26.07%, Kalyan Jewellers 24.63%, P N Gadgil 23.21%, Manoj Vaibhav 14.82% and PC Jeweller 10.32%; prior-year RoNW was 19.73% (FY25) and 24.16% (FY24), so the FY26 reading is one year old.

Store-level throughput is the highest in the disclosed peer set: revenue from operations per store Rs 3,167.56 mn (FY24), Rs 2,816.22 mn (FY25), Rs 4,102.28 mn (FY26) and operating EBITDA per store Rs 128.33 / 123.39 / 274.34 mn, against Rs 419.40 to Rs 1,376.81 mn per store for the listed peers in the RHP's own KPI comparison; average store area 10,670.18 sq. ft. across 650,881 sq. ft. and 61 stores at March 31, 2026, with the Vijayawada store at 100,000 sq. ft. and Somajiguda, Hyderabad at 98,210 sq. ft.

Working capital is part-funded interest-free by customers: advances from customers under the 'Dhana Vandhanam' and 'Free-yo-Flexi' 11-month schemes of Rs 19,432.26 mn (11.58% of revenue, FY24), Rs 31,454.10 mn (18.61%, FY25) and Rs 50,427.50 mn (20.15%, FY26), from 473,412 active enrolled customers at March 31, 2026, stated (Source: CRISIL Report) to be the highest advances from customers amongst key organised jewellery players in India in Fiscals 2026 and 2025.

Credit rating moved up rather than down: ICRA A- (FY24) and ICRA A- (Stable) (FY25) to ICRA A (Stable) (FY26) on both the long-term fund-based cash credit and term loan facilities, with the RHP stating the Company has not experienced any downgrade in the last three Fiscals. Debt-to-equity 0.49 / 0.51 / 0.53 and net debt/EBITDA 0.95 / 1.12 / 0.73 across FY24-FY26.

No pledge and no overhang instruments: nil shares pledged, nil non-disposal undertakings and nil other encumbrances for both Promoter & Promoter Group and Public categories on the beneficiary position as on August 7, 2026; no employee stock option or stock appreciation rights scheme, and no outstanding convertible securities or warrants.

The direct-tax overhang that carried an FY24 auditor emphasis of matter of Rs 10,860.67 mn has closed: ITAT directed the Assessing Officer on June 12, 2025 to delete the demands before it, and in November 2025 the Madras High Court dismissed the Income Tax Department's appeal on Section 68 / 56(2)(viib) additions for AY 2012-13 to AY 2015-16 where the tax under appeal was Rs 1,076.02 mn; outstanding direct-tax litigation thereafter aggregates Rs 14.19 mn.

Manufacturing is in-house rather than bought-in: 816 Karigars on exclusive arrangements and on the rolls at March 31, 2026 (672 with the Company, 144 with subsidiary Asita Jewellery Manufacturing Private Limited) plus 296 on short-term non-exclusive agreements, together manufacturing 79.78% (FY24), 80.66% (FY25) and 79.11% (FY26) of total products available for sale, across facilities of approximately 43,861.96 sq. ft. (Thirumudivakkam, operations commenced December 2, 2024) and 20,000 sq. ft. (Maraimalainagar).

The revenue base has shifted toward the smaller cities the Company targets: Tier II revenue Rs 52,566.99 mn (FY24) to Rs 66,654.87 mn (FY25) to Rs 101,678.67 mn (FY26) and Tier III Rs 31,320.91 / 33,384.08 / 49,089.84 mn, so Tier II at 40.63% of FY26 revenue now exceeds Tier I at 39.75% (50.03% in FY24), with 45 of 61 stores in Tier II and Tier III contributing 60.25% of revenue.

The disclosed compliance tail is small and affirmatively nil in most categories: total contingent liabilities Rs 560.35 mn at March 31, 2026, stated in the RHP as approximately 1.85% of net worth; nil criminal, statutory/regulatory, SEBI/stock-exchange and material civil proceedings against the Company; all categories nil for Directors other than Promoters and for KMP/Senior Management; and nil pending, expired or un-applied-for material approvals for the Company, its 61 stores and its manufacturing facility.

Low fixed-capital intensity: net fixed assets Rs 2,850.29 mn and capital work in progress Rs 236.79 mn at March 31, 2026 against revenue from operations of Rs 250,239.27 mn, with only three of 61 stores owned and the remainder, plus the Registered and Corporate Offices, on leave-and-licence.
